backlog.title: Rewind/Shrink/Audit Edge-Case Correctness (TEST_RESULTS.md mini-PRD)
backlog.description: Fix the five bugs found by adversarial filterPipeline/tool probes (BUG-001…BUG-005). All live in the rewind/shrink targeting + protection layer: two MAJOR rewind-protection failures (to_previous_prompt silently no-ops; checkpoint-crosses-latest partially applies), two MINOR composition defects (live last_tool_call_group fallback inverts; by_content_includes multi-shrink violates last-wins), and one COSMETIC bloat-threshold operator mismatch. The prior round's 8 bugs (config wiring, branch scoping, null-checks, audit suggestion) are already fixed in source — this phase is purely the new round. Implicit-TDD throughout: each subtask writes the failing test → implements → passes. Success = the full 697-test suite stays GREEN with the fixed behavior, plus new content-asserting regression tests for every bug.

milestones.title: Major rewind-protection correctness (BUG-001, BUG-002)
milestones.description: The two MAJOR bugs share one correctness surface: protectedOk() + filterPipeline's `if (!protectedOk(...))` block + rewind.ts step 5b. BUG-001 makes to_previous_prompt:true (2+ users) actually hide the latest user. BUG-002 makes a checkpoint crossing the latest user refuse cleanly (tool) and no-op (filter) instead of partially applying. Sequenced BUG-001-first (changes the protectedOk signature that BUG-002's tool-side guard then reuses). The end state is honest bookkeeping: the tool's reported K always equals the filter's actual hidden count for EVERY granularity.

tasks.title: BUG-001 — to_previous_prompt last_turn must actually hide the latest user (2+ users)
tasks.description: The resolver (resolveLastTurn) already correctly computes the nuclear removal set including iLastUser for the 2+-user case (transforms.test.ts:566 proves remove===[3,4,5]). The filter undoes it: protectedOk() unconditionally protects the latest user with no awareness of to_previous_prompt. Fix: give protectedOk a to_previous_prompt exemption (skip protectLatestUser when the marker explicitly opted in), thread rw.options.to_previous_prompt from filterPipeline, and prove end-to-end via a content-asserting pipeline regression test. Single-user nuclear stays refused by the resolver (iFirstUser===iLastUser) — unaffected.

subtasks.title: protectedOk gains a to_previous_prompt exemption; filterPipeline threads it from the marker
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bugfix_round2_findings.md §1 BUG-001 + §3 step 1. protectedOk() (src/transforms.ts) currently receives ONLY (messages, remove, config) and computes protectLatestUser purely from config.rewind.protectedRoles (default includes 'latest:user'); it returns false whenever remove contains iLatestUser. resolveLastTurn ALREADY refuses the 1-user nuclear case (returns {remove:[]} when iFirstUser===iLastUser) — so protectedOk is the ONLY thing blocking the legitimate 2+-user nuclear rewind. protectFirstUser is a SEPARATE block and MUST be left intact (nuclear never removes the first user; the resolver guarantees iFirstUser<iLastUser for the 2+-user case).
2. INPUT: src/transforms.ts exports protectedOk(messages, remove, config) and filterPipeline(messages, markers, config, branchEntries). The persisted marker shape is RewindMarkerLike (src/transforms.ts): { seq, granularity, options?: { to_previous_prompt?: boolean }, excludeToolCallId?, checkpoint?, hideEntryIds? }. options.to_previous_prompt is the persisted snake_case field the filter reads.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add an OPTIONAL 4th param to protectedOk: `to_previousPrompt?: boolean` (default false/undefined — fully backward-compatible; every existing caller that omits it behaves identically). When `to_previous_prompt === true`, SKIP the entire protectLatestUser block (the marker explicitly asked to shed the latest user; the resolver already refused the 1-user/first-user case). protectFirstUser stays UNCONDITIONAL. (b) In filterPipeline's rewind loop, compute `const nuclear = readOwn(rw, 'options') is a record with to_previous_prompt === true` (read rw.options?.to_previous_prompt === true defensively via readOwn) and pass it as the 4th arg to the existing `protectedOk(m, remove, config, nuclear)` call. Do NOT touch the hideEntryIds pin arm, the resolver functions, or applyRewind. MOCKING: none — transforms.ts is PURE / Pi-Free (0 imports); unit-test directly.
4. OUTPUT: protectedOk preserves its current behavior for to_previous_prompt !== true (all existing protectedOk tests in test/transforms.test.ts + test/pipeline.test.ts stay GREEN unchanged); when true, a removal set containing iLatestUser is ALLOWED (returns true). filterPipeline now honors a 2+-user nuclear last_turn marker. DOCS: update the protectedOk + filterPipeline JSDoc comments in src/transforms.ts to document the new param + the to_previous_prompt exemption (Mode A — per-file docs ride with the work).

tasks.title: BUG-002 — checkpoint crossing the latest user must refuse (tool) / no-op (filter), not partially apply (trim)
tasks.description: filterPipeline has a checkpoint-specific branch that TRIMS the removal set (remove.filter(r => r < iLatestUser)) when protectedOk fails, producing a non-contiguous view and a tool/filter K mismatch. Fix BOTH sides: (filter) remove the trim branch so a checkpoint crossing the latest user no-ops like every other granularity; (tool) add a pre-persist honest-K guard so resolvePreview's reported K always equals what the filter will actually hide — refuse before persisting when a checkpoint removal crosses the latest user. Depends on P1.M1.T1.S1 (the protectedOk signature it reuses).

subtasks.title: filterPipeline: remove the checkpoint-trim branch — checkpoint-crosses-latest now no-ops
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bugfix_round2_findings.md §1 BUG-002 + §3 step 2. The offending code is filterPipeline's `if (!protectedOk(m, remove, config)) { if (granularity === 'checkpoint') { ...iLatestUser...; remove = remove.filter((r) => r < iLatestUser); if (remove.length === 0) continue; } else { continue; } }`. This is the ONLY place a rewind partially applies. PRD §6 step 6 + §8 require a rewind that removes the latest user to be REFUSED/no-op, never trimmed.
2. INPUT: The post-P1.M1.T1.S1 filterPipeline (protectedOk now takes the to_previous_prompt flag; checkpoint markers never set it so protectedOk behaves as before for checkpoint). The filterPipeline rewind loop, the protectedOk call, and the applyRewind/origIdxOfM maintenance are all in scope.
3. LOGIC: Delete the entire `if (granularity === 'checkpoint') { ...trim... }` branch so the block collapses to the single `else { continue; }` path: ANY granularity whose removal set fails protectedOk is SKIPPED wholesale (no partial application, no non-contiguous view). Checkpoint rewinds that do NOT cross the latest user are UNAFFECTED (protectedOk passes → applyRewind proceeds normally). Do NOT change resolveCheckpoint, the hideEntryIds pin arm, or the non-checkpoint branches. MOCKING: none — pure transform.
4. OUTPUT: filterPipeline on the BUG-002 reproduction fixture (msgs len 10, checkpoint 'cp' targeting before the latest user) returns the input UNCHANGED (length 10) instead of length 7. Non-crossing checkpoint rewinds still hide correctly. DOCS: update the filterPipeline JSDoc to state checkpoint rewinds that cross the latest user are skipped (no-op), matching the non-checkpoint granularities (Mode A).

subtasks.title: rewind.ts: pre-persist honest-K guard — refuse when a checkpoint removal crosses the latest user
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bugfix_round2_findings.md §3 step 3 (unified honest-bookkeeping architecture) + §1 BUG-002. rewind.ts step 5b already refuses the 1-user nuclear last_turn (K===0). The SAME pattern must guard checkpoint: after resolvePreview computes `remove`, if the filter's protectedOk would reject that removal set, the tool must REFUSE before renderNote/persist so the reported K never lies. This closes the tool/filter K mismatch for checkpoint AND future-proofs every granularity (reported K === actual hidden count).
2. INPUT: src/tools/rewind.ts rewindExecute — step 5 runs resolvePreview(ctx, params, toolCallId) yielding { ledger, k, hideEntryIds, remove, messages }. Import protectedOk from ../transforms.js (already imports partitionIntoUnits/resolveLastToolCallGroup/resolveLastTurn/resolveCheckpoint). The ProtectedConfig slice protectedOk reads is { rewind: { protectedRoles } } — available via getConfig().rewind.protectedRoles. P1.M1.T1.S1 gave protectedOk the optional 4th to_previous_prompt param (pass params.to_previous_prompt === true so a legitimate 2+-user nuclear last_turn is NOT refused here — the filter now honors it; only checkpoint / genuinely-crossing removals refuse).
3. LOGIC: In rewindExecute, immediately AFTER the resolvePreview try/catch block and BEFORE step (5b), add: `if (!protectedOk(messages, remove, { rewind: { protectedRoles: config.rewind.protectedRoles } }, params.to_previous_prompt === true)) { return refusal('would cross a protected message (checkpoint target is at or before the latest user — rewinding would shed the current ask)', granularity); }`. This runs ONLY when resolvePreview succeeded (messages is non-empty); on the catch fallback (messages=[]) the existing K=0 path + step 5b already handle it. Reuse the existing refusal() helper (it adds the 'Mulligan: refused — ….' envelope + details). Do NOT change resolvePreview itself, appendRewindMarker, leaveNote, or the success path. NOTE: this also makes the 2+-user nuclear last_turn case honest — protectedOk now passes it (S1 fix), so it proceeds to success with a truthful K; only the genuinely-crossing checkpoint refuses. MOCKING: unit-test makeRewindTool(fakePi) against a fakePi/fakeCtx (existing harness in test/tools/rewind.test.ts: makePi, makeCtx, msgEntry, firstText); build a branch whose checkpoint label targets an entry BEFORE the latest user message; assert the tool REFUSES (text contains 'would cross a protected message'), NO marker is appended (appended.length===0), and NO note is sent.
4. OUTPUT: rewindExecute refuses (no marker, no note, refusal details) for a checkpoint crossing the latest user; succeeds with truthful K for a checkpoint NOT crossing the latest user and for a 2+-user nuclear last_turn. DOCS: update the rewind.ts step-5b comment block to document the generalized protectedOk guard (Mode A).

milestones.title: Minor composition correctness (BUG-003, BUG-004)
milestones.description: The two MINOR bugs affect edge-case composition of multiple markers. BUG-003: the LIVE (unpinned) last_tool_call_group fallback inverts under sequential rewinds because it excludes only the current marker's own call, not all rewind calls. BUG-004: by_content_includes multi-shrink violates E17 'last wins' because each shrink re-resolves against the already-substituted working list. Both touch filterPipeline but in disjoint branches (the last_tool_call_group resolver call vs the shrink loop). Merge-ordered after M1.

tasks.title: BUG-003 — live last_tool_call_group fallback composes correctly across multiple rewinds
tasks.description: The hideEntryIds PIN path is correct (pipeline.test.ts:695). The LIVE fallback (resolveLastToolCallGroup called with only the current marker's excludeToolCallId) inverts: rewind#1 sheds rewind#2's confirmation and vice-versa. Fix: collect ALL rewind excludeToolCallIds into a Set once in filterPipeline and pass it to resolveLastToolCallGroup so the live fallback never re-targets another rewind's own group.

subtasks.title: resolveLastToolCallGroup takes the set of all rewind excludeToolCallIds; filterPipeline passes it; flip the LIVE-fallback test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bugfix_round2_findings.md §1 BUG-003 + §3 step 4 + §4 (the LIVE-fallback test at pipeline.test.ts:~720 currently ASSERTS the buggy inversion as documentation and MUST be rewritten). resolveLastToolCallGroup(units, messages, excludeToolCallId?) only skips the CURRENT marker's own group; resolvePreview (rewind.ts) uses the singular form for its single-call preview and must keep working.
2. INPUT: src/transforms.ts exports resolveLastToolCallGroup(units, messages, excludeToolCallId?). filterPipeline's rewind loop calls it in the `else if (granularity === 'last_tool_call_group')` live-fallback branch. rewind.ts resolvePreview also calls the singular form.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add an OPTIONAL 4th param to resolveLastToolCallGroup: `excludeToolCallIds?: Set<string>` (a set of tool-call ids to ALSO skip). In the exclusion step, skip a toolGroup when its assistant issued the singular excludeToolCallId OR any id in excludeToolCallIds (reuse the existing assistantIssuedCall helper — iterate the set). Keep the singular param for resolvePreview's single-call usage (backward compat). (b) In filterPipeline, BEFORE the rewind loop, compute `const allRewindCallIds = new Set(rewinds.map(rw => readOwn(rw,'excludeToolCallId')).filter(id => typeof id==='string' && id.length>0))` ONCE (stableSortBySeq is already applied to `rewinds` — compute from that sorted list). Pass it as the 4th arg in the live-fallback call: `resolveLastToolCallGroup(units, m, excludeId, allRewindCallIds)`. Do NOT change the hideEntryIds pin arm or the other granularities. MOCKING: none — pure transform.
4. OUTPUT: filterPipeline on the BUG-003 fixture (two last_tool_call_group rewinds, NO hideEntryIds) now HIDES both mistake spans (BIG-GREP, BIG-READ absent) and KEEPS both rewind confirmations — matching the PIN-path result and spec §11. Roles become [user, assistant, toolResult, assistant, toolResult, custom, assistant, toolResult] (both mistakes shed, both rewind groups survive). DOCS: update resolveLastToolCallGroup + filterPipeline JSDoc (Mode A). Update test/pipeline.test.ts:~720 LIVE-fallback test: REWRITE it to assert the corrected behavior (both mistake spans absent, both rewind confirmations present, expectNoOrphans). Remove the now-false comment 'documents WHY hideEntryIds exists' and replace with the corrected composition assertion.

tasks.title: BUG-004 — by_content_includes multi-shrink satisfies E17 'last wins'
tasks.description: Two by_content_includes shrinks on the same target: the second silently no-ops because the first shrink's substitution removes the needle from the working list. Fix: resolve ALL shrink targets against the ORIGINAL pre-shrink message list (stable indices) before applying any substitution, then apply by index in seq order (last-wins naturally for same-index; different indices both apply). Safe for all three matchers (shrinks never remove messages or change role/toolCallId/toolName).

subtasks.title: filterPipeline shrink loop resolves targets against the ORIGINAL messages so by_content_includes last-wins
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/bugfix_round2_findings.md §1 BUG-004 + §3 step 5 + the invariant note. applyShrink(messages, marker) calls resolveShrinkTarget(messages, target) against the CURRENT working list; filterPipeline applies shrinks oldest-first via `for (const sh of stableSortBySeq(shrinks)) { m = applyShrink(m, sh); }`. KEY INVARIANT: shrinks never REMOVE messages and never change role/toolCallId/toolName (applyShrink spreads {...orig, content}). So by_tool_call_id and by_tool_name are INVARIANT under shrink; only by_content_includes is sensitive. Resolving every shrink target against the ORIGINAL pre-shrink list is therefore SAFE and CORRECT for all three matchers and fixes by_content_includes.
2. INPUT: src/transforms.ts exports applyShrink(messages, {target, replacement}) and resolveShrinkTarget(messages, target). filterPipeline's shrink loop (after the rewind loop, `m` is the post-rewind working list). The ORIGINAL pre-shrink list is `m` at the START of the shrink loop (rewinds have already gap-closed it, but NO shrink has run yet — that is the correct 'original' for shrink-target resolution).
3. LOGIC: Rewrite the shrink loop to a TWO-PHASE apply: (PHASE 1) snapshot `const shrinkBase = m;` (the post-rewind, pre-shrink list). For each shrink `sh` in stableSortBySeq(shrinks), compute `const idx = resolveShrinkTarget(shrinkBase, sh.target)` against shrinkBase ONCE and record {idx, replacement: sh.replacement} (skip/null/out-of-range → skip). (PHASE 2) apply substitutions to `m` by INDEX: for each recorded {idx, replacement} in seq order, set `m[idx] = {...m[idx], content:[{type:'text', text:replacement}]}` (reuse applyShrink's substitution shape — role/toolCallId preserved via spread; last-wins naturally because later same-index writes overwrite earlier ones; different indices all apply). Build a NEW array (m.map with an index→replacement plan) rather than mutating in place, to keep purity. Guard idx against m.length (a prior rewind could have removed the targeted index in pathological compositions — if idx >= m.length, skip that shrink). Keep applyShrink + resolveShrinkTarget EXPORTED and UNCHANGED (other callers + unit tests depend on them); only filterPipeline's shrink loop changes. NEVER throws (E13). MOCKING: none — pure transform.
4. OUTPUT: filterPipeline on the BUG-004 fixture (two by_content_includes:'NEEDLE' shrinks, replacements 'SHRUNK VERSION ONE' then 'TWO') → the matched toolResult content is 'SHRUNK VERSION TWO' (second wins). Existing by_tool_call_id/by_tool_name multi-shrink + single-shrink tests stay GREEN (same behavior, just resolved against the stable base). DOCS: update the filterPipeline shrink-loop JSDoc to document the two-phase resolve-against-original design and why it is safe for all matchers (Mode A).

milestones.title: Audit / reminder threshold consistency (BUG-005)
milestones.description: COSMETIC off-by-one: the bloat-reminder nudge fires at bytes >= threshold (inclusive) while the audit bloaty flag uses strict > (exclusive). At exactly 8192 bytes the reminder fires but the audit row is unflagged, breaking the feedback loop. Fully isolated to audit.ts + nudges.ts — may be done in parallel with the entire M1/M2 chain.
